record_checkName.message: Its name, as screen readers announce it
record_checkName.description: “Check an element” dialog: a choice in “What to check”: the element’s accessible name.

record_checkVisible.description: “Check an element” dialog: a choice in “What to check”, for an element that is visible. “It” is the element (masculine in French).

record_checkHidden.description: “Check an element” dialog: a choice in “What to check”, for an element that is hidden.

record_checkEnabled.message: It is usable, not grayed out
record_checkEnabled.description: “Check an element” dialog: a choice in “What to check”, for an element that can be used (enabled). Same words as the bug report’s states.

record_checkDisabled.message: It is grayed out, not usable
record_checkDisabled.description: “Check an element” dialog: a choice in “What to check”, for an element that cannot be used (disabled). Same words as the bug report’s states.

record_checkExpected.description: “Check an element” dialog: label of the field holding the value the check expects, filled with what the page shows now.

record_checkAddressLabel.message: The address the page should be on
record_checkAddressLabel.description: “Check the address” dialog: label of the field holding the address the page should be on, filled with the current one.

record_checkAddressEmpty.message: Type the address the page should be on.
record_checkAddressEmpty.description: “Check the address” dialog: shown when the address field is empty.

record_checkAdd.description: The main button of the “Check an element” and “Check the address” dialogs.

record_checkNoLocator.message: No locator finds this element alone: pick another one.
record_checkNoLocator.description: “Check an element” dialog: shown when no locator finds the picked element alone, so the check could not run.

record_lastLocator.description: Recorder HUD: small uppercase heading above the locator of the element the last step acted on.

record_matchingFunctions.description: Recorder HUD: small uppercase heading above the project’s test functions that look like the steps recorded so far.

record_noMatch.description: Recorder HUD, under “Matching test functions”, while none of the project’s test functions looks like the steps recorded so far.

record_matchReady.description: Recorder HUD: small badge next to a test function whose steps were all recorded, so the exported test can call it. One short word (French: agrees with “fonction”).

record_stepNotSaved.message: A step could not be saved.
record_stepNotSaved.description: Recorder HUD, in red: saving the last recorded step failed.

record_storageFull.message: No room left to save steps: stop now and export what you have. New steps are lost.
record_storageFull.description: Recorder HUD, in red: the browser’s storage for the recording is full, so the steps recorded from now on are not kept.

record_reviewLabel.description: Recorder review panel: accessible name of the dialog that opens when a recording stops (read by screen readers, not shown).

record_testTitle.description: Recorder review panel: label of the text field at the top that names the test: the generated spec's test('…') and the steps file's title. Filled with the first page's title. Short.

record_testTitlePlaceholder.description: Recorder review panel: placeholder of the “Test title” field, shown only when no title can be made from the steps.

record_nothingRecorded.description: Recorder review panel: title when the recording has no step.

record_stepsRecorded_one.description: Recorder review panel: title, how many steps the recording has.

record_stepsRecorded_other.description: Recorder review panel: title, how many steps the recording has.

record_stepsMatched_one.message: $count$ step matches one of your test functions
record_stepsMatched_one.description: Recorder review panel: line under the title when some steps will be written as calls to the project’s test functions in the exported code.

record_stepsMatched_other.description: Recorder review panel: line under the title when some steps will be written as calls to the project’s test functions in the exported code.

record_noFunctionMatches.message: None of your test functions match: the code uses locators only.
record_noFunctionMatches.description: Recorder review panel: line under the title when the project has test functions but none matches the steps.

record_notConnected.message: Not connected to Piwi: the code uses locators only.
record_notConnected.description: Recorder review panel: line under the title when Piwi Picker is not connected to a Piwi instance, so it knows no test function.

record_noSteps.description: Recorder review panel: body when the recording has no step.

record_copyCode.description: Recorder review panel: main button, copies the recording as the code of a Playwright test.

record_copyCodeWithFunctions.description: Recorder review panel: main button when connected to Piwi: copies the code of a Playwright test that calls the project’s test functions where the steps match them.

record_copyCodeWithoutFunctions.message: Copy as TypeScript without your functions
record_copyCodeWithoutFunctions.description: Recorder review panel: button that copies the code with plain locators only, even where a test function matches.

record_downloadSteps.description: Recorder review panel: button that saves the recording as a steps file (JSON).

record_downloadStepsTitle.message: Saves the recording as a steps file, to share it or turn it into a test with piwi codegen
record_downloadStepsTitle.description: Recorder review panel: tooltip of “Download steps”. “piwi codegen” is a command: keep it as it is.

record_sendToEditor.description: Button in the recording review: the paired editor renders the recorded steps as the body of a test, with the project’s functions, and inserts it at the cursor.

record_replay.description: Recorder review panel: button that plays the recorded steps again on the site, before they are exported. Short.

record_replayHint.message: Play the steps again on this site, with a cursor, and see that each step still finds its element

bug_reportLabel.description: Report a bug: aria-label of the HUD shown while a bug is recorded, and of the finished report panel.

bug_hudTitle_one.description: Report a bug: title of the small box in the page corner while the steps are recorded. $count$ is the number of steps so far. Short: one line.

bug_hudTitle_other.description: Report a bug: title of the small box in the page corner while the steps are recorded. $count$ is the number of steps so far. Short: one line.

bug_mark.description: Report a bug: button that lets the tester pick an element on the page and say what it should show. Also the title of the dialog it opens, and quoted in other messages.

bug_markHint.message: Choose an element on the page and say what it should show
bug_markHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of the “Mark what’s wrong” button.

bug_missing.description: Report a bug: button to name an element that should be on the page and is not. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

bug_missingHint.message: Name an element that should be on this page and is not
bug_missingHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of the “Something is missing” button.

bug_wrongPage.description: Report a bug: button to say the steps ended on the wrong page. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

bug_wrongPageHint.message: Say which page you should have reached
bug_wrongPageHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of the “Wrong page” button.

bug_screenshot.description: Report a bug: HUD button that takes a screenshot of the page now, shown while Chrome's debugging protocol takes them. Short.

bug_screenshotHint.message: Add a screenshot of the page as it is now
bug_screenshotHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of the HUD's Screenshot button.

bug_debuggingOn.message: Chrome shows a bar saying Piwi Picker started debugging this browser: that is this report reading the console, the failed requests and screenshots. Nothing leaves your computer, and the bar goes when you finish.
bug_debuggingOn.description: Report a bug: HUD line while Chrome's debugging protocol collects the evidence. Chrome's own bar says the extension started debugging the browser.

bug_debuggingCanceled.message: The debugging bar was cancelled: the report reads the console and the requests from the page from now on, and a screenshot needs "$action$" in Piwi Picker.
bug_debuggingCanceled.description: Report a bug: HUD line after the person cancelled Chrome's debugging bar. $action$ is the name of the popup's “Take a screenshot” button.

bug_debuggingRefused.message: Chrome refused the debugging session (another debugger on this tab, or a policy): the report reads the console and the requests from the page, and a screenshot needs "$action$" in Piwi Picker.
bug_debuggingRefused.description: Report a bug: HUD line when Chrome refused or ended the debugging session. $action$ is the name of the popup's “Take a screenshot” button.

bug_finish.description: Report a bug: button that stops recording and opens the finished report.

bug_screenshotBlocked.message: Chrome lets Piwi Picker take a screenshot only after you open it on this tab. Open Piwi Picker and choose "$action$".
bug_screenshotBlocked.description: Report a bug: warning when no screenshot could be taken. $action$ is the name of the popup’s “Take a screenshot” button.

bug_screenshotBlockedFirefox.message: Firefox lets Piwi Picker take a screenshot only after you open it on this tab. Open Piwi Picker and choose "$action$".
bug_screenshotBlockedFirefox.description: Report a bug, in Firefox: warning when no screenshot could be taken without the grant opening Piwi Picker on the tab gives. $action$ is the name of the popup’s “Take a screenshot” button.

bug_screenshotNotInFront.message: The tab was not the one in front, and the browser captures only the tab on screen.
bug_screenshotNotInFront.description: Report a bug: why there is no screenshot when the recorded tab was in the background. A sentence, also shown after “No screenshot:”.

bug_screenshotFailed.message: The browser could not take the screenshot.
bug_screenshotFailed.description: Report a bug: why there is no screenshot when the browser failed to take it for another reason. A sentence, also shown after “No screenshot:”.

bug_screenshotNotKept.message: The screenshot was too large to keep in this browser’s storage.
bug_screenshotNotKept.description: Report a bug: warning when a screenshot was taken but session storage had no room left for it, so the report has none.

bug_stepShows.description: Report a bug: after a marked step, what the page showed. $text$ is the page’s text, as it is.

bug_stepIs.description: Report a bug: after a marked step, the state the element was in. $state$ is one of the bug_state* words (visible, hidden, usable, grayed out).

bug_stepAbsent.description: Report a bug: after a step saying an element is missing: the page does not have it.

bug_stateVisible.description: Report a bug: an element’s state, in “is $state$” and “The page shows”.

bug_stateHidden.description: Report a bug: an element’s state (not visible), in “is $state$” and “The page shows”. French: masculine (un élément).

bug_stateEnabled.description: Report a bug: an element’s state (enabled), in “is $state$” and “The page shows”.

bug_stateDisabled.description: Report a bug: an element’s state (disabled, cannot be used), in “is $state$” and “The page shows”. French: masculine (un élément).

bug_addToReport.description: Report a bug: the main button of each dialog.

bug_onElement.description: Report a bug, “Mark what’s wrong” dialog: under the title, the locator of the chosen element. $locator$ is Playwright code, never translated.

bug_whatsWrong.description: Report a bug, “Mark what’s wrong” dialog: label of the list of what can be wrong with the element.

bug_itsValue.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”: the value of a field.

bug_itsText.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”: the text the element shows.

bug_itsName.message: Its name, as screen readers announce it
bug_itsName.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”: the element’s accessible name.

bug_shouldBeVisible.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”, for an element that is hidden. “It” is the element (masculine in French).

bug_shouldBeHidden.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”, for an element that is visible.

bug_shouldBeEnabled.message: It should be usable, not grayed out
bug_shouldBeEnabled.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”, for an element that is disabled.

bug_shouldBeDisabled.message: It should be grayed out, not usable
bug_shouldBeDisabled.description: Report a bug: a choice in “What’s wrong”, for an element that is enabled.

bug_pageShows.description: Report a bug, “Mark what’s wrong” dialog: label above what the element shows now.

bug_shouldShow.description: Report a bug, “Mark what’s wrong” dialog: label of the field where the tester types the expected value or text.

bug_note.description: Report a bug: label of the optional free-text note in each dialog.

bug_notePlaceholder.description: Report a bug: placeholder of the note field.

bug_sameAsPage.message: That is what the page shows now. Type what it should show instead.
bug_sameAsPage.description: Report a bug, “Mark what’s wrong” dialog: error when the expected value is the one the page already shows.

bug_whatShouldBeThere.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: label of the list of element kinds.

bug_itsNameLabel.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: label of the field for the missing element’s name.

bug_namePlaceholder.message: Its name as it reads on the page: Download invoice
bug_namePlaceholder.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: placeholder of the name field, with an example after the colon.

bug_nameRequired.message: Type its name, as it would read on the page.
bug_nameRequired.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: error when the name is empty.

bug_alreadyThere_one.message: $count$ element like this is already on the page: use "$mark$" to say what is wrong with it.
bug_alreadyThere_one.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: error when the named element is on the page. $count$ is how many were found (1 or more); $mark$ is the name of the “Mark what’s wrong” button.

bug_alreadyThere_other.message: $count$ elements like this are already on the page: use "$mark$" to say what is wrong with them.
bug_alreadyThere_other.description: Report a bug, “Something is missing” dialog: error when the named element is on the page. $count$ is how many were found (1 or more); $mark$ is the name of the “Mark what’s wrong” button.

bug_youAreOn.description: Report a bug, “Wrong page” dialog: under the title, the address of the current page. $path$ is the page’s path, as it is.

bug_pageShouldBe.message: The page you should be on
bug_pageShouldBe.description: Report a bug, “Wrong page” dialog: label of the field for the expected address.

bug_samePage.message: That is the address of this page. Type the one you should have reached.
bug_samePage.description: Report a bug, “Wrong page” dialog: error when the expected address is the current one.

bug_kindButton.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindLink.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindHeading.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”: a heading.

bug_kindTextbox.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindCombobox.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindCheckbox.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindRadio.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindOption.message: Choice in a dropdown or a list
bug_kindOption.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”: an option.

bug_kindTab.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”: a tab of a tabbed panel.

bug_kindMenuitem.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindListitem.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindRow.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindCell.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindImg.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindDialog.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindAlert.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindStatus.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_kindRegion.description: Report a bug: a kind of element in “What should be there”.

bug_finishTitle_one.description: Report a bug: title of the finished report panel. $count$ is the number of steps.

bug_finishTitle_other.description: Report a bug: title of the finished report panel. $count$ is the number of steps.

bug_title.description: Report a bug, finished report: label of the report’s title field.

bug_titlePlaceholder.message: What’s wrong, in a few words: Coupon not applied to the total
bug_titlePlaceholder.description: Report a bug, finished report: placeholder of the title field, with an example after the colon.

bug_attached.description: Report a bug, finished report: what was collected besides the steps. $summary$ is a list such as “2 screenshots · 1 console error”, in the interface language.

bug_stepShots.description: Report a bug, finished report: checkbox, on by default, that keeps in the report the screenshot of the page as each step began. $count$ is how many were taken.

bug_stepShotsHint.message: The page as each step began, for whoever plays a step by hand. They show the whole page: leave them out if it shows what should not be shared.
bug_stepShotsHint.description: Report a bug, finished report: under the step screenshots checkbox, what they are for and why to leave them out.

bug_nothingMarked.message: Nothing is marked as wrong, so the test would pass. Record again and use "$mark$".
bug_nothingMarked.description: Report a bug, finished report: warning when no step says what is wrong. $mark$ is the name of the “Mark what’s wrong” button.

bug_stepWarning.description: Report a bug, finished report: a warning about one step of the generated test. $message$ is the code generator’s warning, in English.

message.example: no stable locator for this element

bug_noScreenshot.description: Report a bug, finished report: warning when the report has no screenshot. $reason$ says why, as a sentence.

reason.example: Chrome lets Piwi Picker take a screenshot only after you open it on this tab.

bug_noScreenshotTaken.description: Report a bug, finished report: warning when the report has no screenshot, for no known reason.

bug_copyTest.description: Report a bug, finished report: button that copies a Playwright test that fails while the bug is there.

bug_copyTestHint.message: A Playwright test that fails while the bug is there, marked with test.fail()
bug_copyTestHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of “Copy failing test”. test.fail() is code, never translated.

bug_copyReport.description: Report a bug, finished report: button that copies the report as Markdown.

bug_copyReportHint.message: The report as Markdown, for a ticket or a message
bug_copyReportHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of “Copy report”.

bug_downloadReport.description: Report a bug, finished report: button that downloads every file of the report as one .piwibug file, a zip archive that Piwi Picker’s Replay and the Piwi desktop app open. “.piwibug” is a file extension, kept as it is.

bug_downloadReportHint.message: steps.json, the test, the report in Markdown, evidence.json and the screenshots, in one zip archive
bug_downloadReportHint.description: Report a bug: tooltip of “Download .piwibug”: the files in the archive. File names are never translated.

bug_replay.description: Report a bug, finished report: button that plays the recorded steps again on the site.

bug_replayHint.message: Play the steps again on this site, with a cursor, and see whether the bug shows

bug_staysLocal.message: Everything here stays in this browser: nothing is sent anywhere.
bug_staysLocal.description: Report a bug, finished report: note at the bottom of the panel.

bug_sendToPiwi.description: Report a bug, finished report: the button that opens the preview of what is sent to the connected Piwi instance.

bug_sendToPiwiHint.message: See exactly what is sent, then store the report on your Piwi instance
bug_sendToPiwiHint.description: Report a bug, finished report: tooltip of “Send to Piwi…”.

bug_sendTitle.description: Send to Piwi preview: dialog title. $project$ is a project name.

bug_sendWhere.message: A bug report of $project$ on $instance$. Only what is ticked below is sent.
bug_sendWhere.description: Send to Piwi preview: first line. $instance$ is a host such as piwi.acme.com, $project$ a project name.

bug_sendFirstTime.message: This is the first report sent from this browser. Piwi Picker sends a report only when you click Send, only to the instance you connected, and only what you tick here. The steps keep the values you typed, except passwords.
bug_sendFirstTime.description: Send to Piwi preview: shown before the first send from this browser profile, to explain what connected mode now sends.

bug_sendSteps_one.message: The title and $count$ step, with the page it was on
bug_sendSteps_one.description: Send to Piwi preview: what is always sent. $count$ is the number of steps.

bug_sendSteps_other.message: The title and $count$ steps, with the pages they were on
bug_sendSteps_other.description: Send to Piwi preview: what is always sent. $count$ is the number of steps.

bug_sendScreenshots.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox. $count$ is a number.

bug_sendStepShots.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox for the screenshot of the page as each step began. $count$ is a number.

bug_sendConsole.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox. $count$ is a number.

bug_sendRequests.message: Failed requests (method, path, status; never a body): $count$
bug_sendRequests.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox. $count$ is a number.

bug_sendOutline.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox for the outline of the page.

bug_sendEnvValues.message: Leave out the values I typed (the test reads them from environment variables)
bug_sendEnvValues.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox that removes every typed value from the steps sent; the generated test then reads them from environment variables.

bug_sendCreateIssue.message: Also create a Jira issue in $project$
bug_sendCreateIssue.description: Send to Piwi preview: checkbox that also files the report in the project’s issue tracker. $project$ is a Jira project key such as SHOP.

bug_sendFilesEvery.message: This project files every bug report in Jira.
bug_sendFilesEvery.description: Send to Piwi preview: under the checkbox, when the project files every report whoever sends it.

bug_issueCreated.description: Send to Piwi: after sending, the Jira issue was created. $key$ is its key such as SHOP-812.

bug_issueQueued.message: The Jira issue is queued: the report’s page shows its key once it is created.
bug_issueQueued.description: Send to Piwi: after sending, the Jira issue is queued and will be created by the instance; the report’s page shows its key once created.

bug_sendShowData.description: Send to Piwi preview: disclosure that shows the JSON that is sent.

bug_send.description: Send to Piwi preview: the button that sends.

bug_sending.description: Send to Piwi preview: while sending.

bug_sent.description: Send to Piwi: after sending. $id$ is the number of the report on the instance.

bug_openInPiwi.description: Send to Piwi: link to the report on the instance, after sending.

bug_sendFailed.description: Send to Piwi: the report was not sent. $error$ is the reason, already translated.

bug_sendNoProject.message: No project of your Piwi instance matches this page. Add this site in the settings, or choose the project in Piwi Picker’s menu.
bug_sendNoProject.description: Send to Piwi: no project of the connected instance applies to this page.

bug_staysLocalUntilSent.message: Everything here stays in this browser until you send it.
bug_staysLocalUntilSent.description: Report a bug, finished report: note at the bottom of the panel when an instance is connected.

replay_hudLabel.message: Piwi Picker: replaying a bug report
replay_hudLabel.description: Replay panel (the box in the corner while a bug report replays): its aria-label, read by screen readers.

replay_statusRunning.description: Replay panel title while the steps play. Short: often followed by “: <report title>”.

replay_statusPaused.description: Replay panel title while the replay is paused. Short.

replay_statusDone.description: Replay panel title once every step has played or the replay stopped. Short.

replay_statusWithTitle.description: Replay panel title when the report has a title. $status$ is Replaying, Paused or Replayed (replay_status*); $title$ is the title the tester gave the report, as written.

replay_progress.description: Replay panel, under the title while it plays. $origin$ is the site the steps replay on; $step$ the step playing now; $total$ how many steps there are.

replay_progressDone_one.description: Replay panel, under the title once the replay is over. $origin$ is the site the steps replayed on.

replay_progressDone_other.description: Replay panel, under the title once the replay is over. $origin$ is the site the steps replayed on.

replay_underConditions.description: Replay panel and DevTools Piwi panel: the request conditions on in the tab when the replay started. $conditions$ lists them, from the devtools_condition* messages.

replay_viewportSet.description: Replay panel: the replay set the tab's viewport to the size the steps were recorded at. $size$ is width×height in CSS pixels, such as 390×844.

replay_viewportDiffers.message: Recorded at $recorded$, played at $actual$: resize the window if the page depends on its size
replay_viewportDiffers.description: Replay panel: the replay could not set the tab's viewport (no debugging protocol, as in Firefox) and the tab's size differs from the recorded one. $recorded$ and $actual$ are width×height in CSS pixels.

replay_pause.description: Replay panel button that pauses the replay. Short.

replay_continue.description: Replay panel button that continues a paused replay. Short.

replay_nextStep.description: Replay panel button, step-by-step mode: plays the next step. Short.

replay_stepByStep.description: Replay panel checkbox: wait for a click on Next step before each step. Short.

replay_again.description: Replay panel button, once the replay is over: plays the same steps again from the start. Short.

replay_stepFound.description: Replay panel, under an expected result that did not hold: what the page showed instead. $found$ is one of replay_found* or a URL.

replay_cursorCheck.description: Caption next to the replay’s fake cursor while it checks an expected result. $step$ is the step in words, in the interface language.

step.example: The element with test id cart-total should show "Total: 42"

replay_cursorNext.description: Caption next to the replay’s fake cursor in step-by-step mode, pointing at the element the next step acts on. $step$ is the step in words, in the interface language.

replay_quotedText.description: A text, value or name read from the page, quoted, as the replay shows what it found. $text$ is the page’s text, as it is. Only the quotes change.

replay_foundMissing.description: What the replay found for an expected result whose element is not on the page. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”).

replay_foundCount_one.description: What the replay found when the step’s locator finds several elements where one was expected. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”).

replay_foundCount_other.description: What the replay found when the step’s locator finds several elements where one was expected. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”).

replay_foundVisible.description: What the replay found: the element is visible. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_foundHidden.description: What the replay found: the element is hidden. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_foundEnabled.description: What the replay found: the element can be used (not disabled). Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_foundDisabled.description: What the replay found: the element is disabled. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_foundChecked.description: What the replay found: the checkbox or switch is checked. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_foundUnchecked.description: What the replay found: the checkbox or switch is not checked. Read after “found” (French: after “Résultat :”, about “l’élément”, masculine).

replay_verdictReproduced.description: Replay verdict title: an expected result of the bug report did not hold on this page, so the bug shows here.

replay_verdictExpectedFound.description: Replay verdict detail when the bug shows. $expected$ is the text the report expected, from the page, as written; $found$ what the page showed (replay_quotedText, replay_found* or a URL).

replay_verdictExpectedFoundAsReported.description: Like replay_verdictExpectedFound, when the page shows exactly what the tester reported.

replay_verdictFound.description: Replay verdict detail when the bug shows and the step expected a state rather than a text (visible, enabled…). $found$ is what the page showed (replay_found*).

replay_verdictFoundAsReported.description: Like replay_verdictFound, when the page shows exactly what the tester reported.

replay_verdictNotReproduced.description: Replay verdict title: every expected result of the bug report holds, so the bug does not show here.

replay_verdictNotReproducedDetail.message: Every expected result holds on this page.

replay_verdictNotReproducedRun.message: Step $step$, where the test failed when it ran, played here.
replay_verdictNotReproducedRun.description: Under the Not reproduced verdict of a report made from a test run: the step where the test failed played here.

replay_verdictDiverged.message: Could not reach the bug: stopped at step $step$
replay_verdictDiverged.description: Replay verdict title when a step could not be done on this page.

replay_verdictDivergedDetail.message: $reason$ This page is not the same as in the report: other data, another account, or an option turned on or off.
replay_verdictDivergedDetail.description: Replay verdict detail when a step could not be done. $reason$ is why, a full sentence (replay_reason*).

reason.example: Nothing on this page matches getByTestId('add-to-cart').

replay_verdictFailedAsInRun.message: Failed at step $step$, as in the test run
replay_verdictFailedAsInRun.description: Replay verdict title when a step could not be done, and it is the step where the test failed in the test run the report was made from.

replay_verdictFailedAsInRunDetail.message: $reason$ The test failed at this same step when it ran.
replay_verdictFailedAsInRunDetail.description: Under replay_verdictFailedAsInRun. $reason$ is why the step could not be done, a sentence.

reason.example: Nothing on this page matches getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).

replay_verdictCompleted.description: Replay verdict title when the steps hold no expected result to check.

replay_verdictCompletedDetail.message: Nothing in these steps says what to expect.
replay_verdictCompletedDetail.description: Replay verdict detail under “Replayed every step”.

replay_verdictStopped.description: Replay verdict title when the tester stopped the replay.

replay_verdictStoppedDetail.description: Replay verdict detail when the tester stopped the replay.

replay_verdictStoppedNoStep.message: The run ended before the last step: it was stopped, or could not start.
replay_verdictStoppedNoStep.description: Run with Playwright dialog: verdict detail under “Stopped” when the desktop app’s run was stopped or could not start, without saying at which step.

replay_reasonNoLocator.message: The report does not say how to find this element.
replay_reasonNoLocator.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the step was recorded without a locator.

replay_reasonNoMatch.description: Why a replay step could not be done. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code.

replay_reasonManyMatches_one.message: $count$ element matches $locator$, and the replay needs exactly one.
replay_reasonManyMatches_one.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the locator finds several elements. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code.

replay_reasonManyMatches_other.message: $count$ elements match $locator$, and the replay needs exactly one.
replay_reasonManyMatches_other.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the locator finds several elements. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code.

replay_reasonHidden.message: $locator$ is on the page, but hidden.
replay_reasonHidden.description: Why a replay step could not be done. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code (French: masculine, “le locator”).

replay_reasonDisabled.description: Why a replay step could not be done. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code (French: masculine).

replay_reasonMoving.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the element never stood still long enough to act on it. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code.

replay_reasonOtherPage.message: This step happened on $expected$, and the tab is on $actual$.
replay_reasonOtherPage.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the tab is on another page. $expected$ and $actual$ are page paths.

replay_startedHere.message: Started from the tab’s page instead.
replay_startedHere.description: Replay panel, under the first step (Go to …) when the replay started on the tab's own page rather than opening the recorded one.

replay_reasonInputInterrupted.message: The action stopped halfway: the debugging session ended after part of it reached the page. The replay stops here rather than doing it twice.
replay_reasonInputInterrupted.description: Why a replay stopped: trusted input was cut off after part of a click, key press or drag had reached the page.

replay_reasonActionFailed.message: The page did not react to the action the way it did when it was recorded.
replay_reasonActionFailed.description: Why a replay step could not be done: the click, typing or choice did not have its effect.

replay_reasonManual.message: The test does this in a way Replay cannot play.
replay_reasonManual.description: Why a step goes to the person: it is a manual step of a steps file made from a test run, which nothing can play.

replay_reasonManualAt.message: The test does this at $location$, in a way Replay cannot play.
replay_reasonManualAt.description: Why a step goes to the person: a manual step of a steps file made from a test run, with where the test does it. $location$ is a file and line, such as tests/cart.spec.ts:12.

replay_reasonCovered.message: $other$ covers $element$ where the pointer would land.
replay_reasonCovered.description: Why a replay step could not be done with trusted input: another element covers the one to click. $element$ and $other$ are a tag and a name from the page, such as button "Apply".

replay_reasonOffscreen.message: $element$ stays outside the visible part of the page.
replay_reasonOffscreen.description: Why a replay step could not be done with trusted input: the element cannot be brought on screen. $element$ is a tag and a name from the page.

replay_reasonDragApart.message: The drag needs $element$ and $target$ on screen at once, and they do not fit together.
replay_reasonDragApart.description: Why a replay's drag step could not be done with trusted input: the element dragged and the one it is dropped on are too far apart to be on screen together. $element$ and $target$ are a tag and a name from the page, such as div "Card".

replay_driverTrusted.message: Played with trusted input, as Playwright sends it. Chrome shows a bar saying Piwi Picker started debugging this browser: that is this replay, and the bar goes when it ends.
replay_driverTrusted.description: Replay panel, under its title and its verdict: the replay acts with trusted input through Chrome's debugging protocol, and Chrome's bar saying the extension is debugging the browser is expected.

replay_driverEventsUnavailable.message: Played with the page’s own events: this browser gives extensions no debugging protocol, so a hover or a drag may not act as a mouse does.
replay_driverEventsUnavailable.description: Replay panel: the replay acts with the page's own events because the browser (Firefox) has no debugging protocol for extensions.

replay_driverEventsRefused.message: Played with the page’s own events: the browser refused the debugging session (another debugger on this tab, a policy, or a page the browser protects).
replay_driverEventsRefused.description: Replay panel: the replay acts with the page's own events because the browser refused the debugging session.

replay_driverEventsCanceled.message: Played with the page’s own events from there on: the debugging bar was cancelled.
replay_driverEventsCanceled.description: Replay panel: the person clicked Cancel on Chrome's debugging bar, so the replay goes on with the page's own events.

replay_driverEventsLost.message: Played with the page’s own events from there on: the debugging session ended.
replay_driverEventsLost.description: Replay panel: the debugging session ended during the replay, which goes on with the page's own events.

replay_stepTrusted.description: Replay panel, at the end of a step's row: the step was done with trusted input. A few words at most.

replay_stepEvents.description: Replay panel, at the end of a step's row: the step was done with the page's own events. A few words at most.

replay_fileAsk_one.message: Step $step$ chooses $count$ file, $files$, which the report names but does not carry. Choose it on this computer to go on, or skip the step.
replay_fileAsk_one.description: Replay panel, while a step that chooses a file waits: the report names the files but does not carry them. $step$ is the step number, $files$ the quoted names, $count$ how many.

replay_fileAsk_other.message: Step $step$ chooses $count$ files, $files$, which the report names but does not carry. Choose them on this computer to go on, or skip the step.
replay_fileAsk_other.description: Replay panel, while a step that chooses a file waits: the report names the files but does not carry them. $step$ is the step number, $files$ the quoted names, $count$ how many.

replay_fileChoose.description: Replay panel: the accessible name of the file chooser a file step shows.

replay_fileSkip.description: Replay panel: the button that leaves a file step out.

replay_fileSkipped.description: Replay panel, under a file step the person skipped.

replay_handOverWhy.message: Step $step$ could not be played here. $reason$
replay_handOverWhy.description: Replay panel: a step the replay could not play, handed to the person. $step$ is its number, $reason$ why it could not be played, a sentence from the replay_reason* messages.

replay_handOverShot.message: The page as step $step$ began, its element outlined
replay_handOverShot.description: Replay panel: alternative text of the screenshot of a step handed to the person. $step$ is its number.

replay_handOverHow.message: Do it yourself on the page, as the screenshot shows, then continue.
replay_handOverHow.description: Replay panel: under the screenshot of a step handed to the person, what to do.

replay_handOverHowNoShot.message: Do it yourself on the page, then continue.
replay_handOverHowNoShot.description: Replay panel: what to do with a step handed to the person when the report has no screenshot of it.

replay_handOverLocators.description: Replay panel, step handed to the person: above the locators the step's element was recorded with, at most three.

replay_handOverDropOn.description: Replay panel, a drag step handed to the person: above the locators of the element it was dropped on.

replay_handOverFound_one.message: $count$ element on this page matches them: outlined.
replay_handOverFound_one.description: Replay panel, step handed to the person: how many elements of the page the recorded locators find now; they are outlined on the page.

replay_handOverFound_other.message: $count$ elements on this page match them: outlined.
replay_handOverFound_other.description: Replay panel, step handed to the person: how many elements of the page the recorded locators find now; they are outlined on the page.

replay_handOverNotFound.message: None of them finds it on this page.
replay_handOverNotFound.description: Replay panel, step handed to the person: none of the recorded locators finds an element on the page now.

replay_handOverDone.description: Replay panel: button the person clicks once they did the handed-over step on the page; the replay goes on with the next step.

replay_handOverSkip.description: Replay panel: button that leaves the handed-over step out and goes on with the next one.

replay_handOverStop.description: Replay panel: button that ends the replay at the handed-over step, which then could not reach the bug.

replay_doneByHand.description: Replay panel: under a step the person did by hand when the replay could not play it.

replay_stepSkipped.description: Replay panel: under a step the person chose to skip when the replay could not play it.

replay_byHand_one.description: Replay panel: under the verdict, the steps the person played by hand. $steps$ lists their numbers, such as 3, 5.

replay_byHand_other.description: Replay panel: under the verdict, the steps the person played by hand. $steps$ lists their numbers, such as 3, 5.

replay_fileChosen.description: Replay panel, under a file step: the files the person chose for it. $files$ is the quoted names.

replay_dialogTitle.description: Title and aria-label of the dialog that chooses which bug report to replay. Same name as the popup’s button (popup_replayBug).

replay_dialogIntro.message: Plays its steps on $origin$, with a cursor showing each one, and says whether the bug shows here.
replay_dialogIntro.description: Replay dialog, under its title. $origin$ is the site of the current tab.

replay_useRecorded.message: Use the bug report recorded in this browser
replay_useRecorded.description: Replay dialog button: replays the last bug report recorded with Piwi Picker in this browser.

replay_useRecordedActions.message: Use the actions recorded in this browser
replay_useRecordedActions.description: Replay dialog button: replays the last recording of actions (Record actions, not a bug report) made with Piwi Picker in this browser.

replay_chooseFile.message: Or choose the report’s .piwibug, or its steps.json, saved by Piwi Picker:
replay_chooseFile.description: Replay dialog, above the file field. “.piwibug” and “steps.json” are file names, kept as they are.

replay_pasteSteps.message: Or paste the text of a steps.json, such as the steps copied from Piwi
replay_pasteSteps.description: Replay dialog, the disclosure that opens a field to paste steps into. “steps.json” is a file name, kept as it is.

replay_pasteLabel.description: Replay dialog, the accessible name of the field steps are pasted into.

replay_pasteUse.description: Replay dialog, the button that reads the pasted steps.

replay_pasteNotSteps.message: The pasted text is not a steps file: $error$
replay_pasteNotSteps.description: Replay dialog, when the pasted text cannot be read. $error$ is the first problem found, in English.

error.example: steps[2].action: is not a known action

replay_fromPiwi.message: Or a bug report of $project$ on Piwi:
replay_fromPiwi.description: Replay chooser: label of the list of bug reports fetched from the connected instance. $project$ is a project name.

replay_fromPiwiChoose.description: Replay chooser: first option of the list of bug reports from the instance.

replay_fromPiwiItem.description: Replay chooser: one bug report from the instance. $id$ is its number, $title$ its title as the reporter wrote it.

title.example: Coupon not applied to the total

replay_fromPiwiNone.message: $project$ has no open bug report on Piwi.
replay_fromPiwiNone.description: Replay chooser: the project mapped to this tab has no open bug report. $project$ is a project name.

replay_fromPiwiFailed.message: Could not read the bug reports from Piwi: $error$
replay_fromPiwiFailed.description: Replay chooser: the list or the report could not be read from the instance. $error$ is the reason, already translated.

replay_runWithPlaywright.description: Replay chooser and finished replay: button that sends the steps to the paired desktop app to run with Playwright.

replay_seenHere.message: What the page showed during the replay:
replay_seenHere.description: Under a replay's verdict: heading above the failed requests and console errors the page showed during the replay.

replay_seenRequest.description: Under a replay's verdict: a request that failed during the replay. $method$ is GET or POST, $url$ its path, $status$ the HTTP status.

replay_seenRequestFailed.description: Under a replay's verdict: a request that got no answer during the replay. $method$ is GET or POST, $url$ its path.

replay_seenConsole.description: Under a replay's verdict: an error the page logged to its console during the replay. $message$ is the page's message, as it is.

replay_seenMore.description: Under a replay's verdict: how many more requests and console errors are not listed. $count$ is a number, already formatted.

replay_share.description: Under a verdict of a report from the connected instance: button that shows what Share result sends, before sending it.

replay_sharePreview.message: Sends to $instance$, on the report: this verdict, the site it ran on ($origin$) and your browser’s name.
replay_sharePreview.description: Share result: exactly what is sent, and where, before sending a replay's verdict. $instance$ is the Piwi instance's host, $origin$ the site the replay ran on.

replay_sharePreviewDesktop.message: Sends to $instance$, on the report: this verdict and your browser’s name.
replay_sharePreviewDesktop.description: Share result: exactly what is sent, and where, before sending the desktop app's verdict. $instance$ is the Piwi instance's host.

replay_shared.description: Share result: the verdict was recorded on the report.

devtools_cpuLabel.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Network tab: label of the select that slows the CPU down. One word.

devtools_throttleNone.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Network tab: the first option of the network and CPU selects, nothing throttled.

devtools_throttleFast3g.description: The whole page's network throttled to DevTools' Fast 3G preset: an option of the Network select, and a line of the conditions on.

devtools_throttleSlow3g.description: The whole page's network throttled to DevTools' Slow 3G preset: an option of the Network select, and a line of the conditions on.

devtools_throttleOffline.description: The whole page offline: an option of the Network select, and a line of the conditions on.

devtools_cpuSlower.description: The CPU slowed down: an option of the CPU select, and a line of the conditions on. $rate$ is how many times slower, such as 4.

devtools_emulationRefused.message: The browser refused the debugging session that throttling needs: $error$
devtools_emulationRefused.description: DevTools, Piwi panel: the network or CPU throttling could not be set because the browser refused the debugging session. $error$ is the browser's words.

error.example: Another debugger is already attached to the tab.

devtools_emulationUnavailable.message: Throttling the whole page needs the debugging protocol, which this browser does not give extensions.
devtools_emulationUnavailable.description: DevTools, Piwi panel: throttling asked for in a browser that gives extensions no debugging protocol (Firefox).

devtools_copyAs.description: DevTools, Piwi sidebar: before the three copy buttons under a locator (common_copyModeBare, common_copyModeAction, common_copyModeExpect). Short.

devtools_tabLocators.description: DevTools, Piwi panel: tab where a locator is typed and the elements it finds are listed. One word.

devtools_tabSession.description: DevTools, Piwi panel: tab listing the named elements of the pick session. One word.

devtools_viewport.description: Piwi panel in DevTools, toolbar button showing or hiding the bar that opens the page at a Playwright project's viewport. One word.

devtools_viewportOpen.description: Piwi panel in DevTools, viewport bar: button opening the inspected page in a new window at the chosen viewport. Short.

devtools_locatorPlaceholder.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: example in the empty locator field. Keep getByLabel('…') as it is; the field's label, Email, may be translated.

devtools_locatorsHint.message: Type a locator: the elements it finds on this page are listed, as Playwright finds them. Hover one to outline it on the page; Reveal selects it in the Elements panel. Enter keeps the locator in the history, which the up and down arrows go through.
devtools_locatorsHint.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: shown while the field is empty.

devtools_matches.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: accessible name of the list of elements the locator finds.

devtools_reveal.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: button beside a found element that selects it in DevTools' Elements panel. One short word.

devtools_revealFailed.message: This element could not be selected in the Elements panel: it may no longer be on the page. Try the locator again.
devtools_revealFailed.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: under the elements found, when Reveal could not select one, most often because the page removed it.

devtools_matchesListed.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Locators tab: under the list, when the locator finds more elements than it lists. $shown$ is how many are listed.

devtools_sessionEmpty.message: No named element yet. Select one in the Elements panel and use Add to session in the Piwi sidebar.
devtools_sessionEmpty.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Session tab: no element has been named yet. “Add to session” is the sidebar's button (devtools_addToSession).

devtools_sessionCount_one.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Session tab: how many elements the session names. $count$ is the number.

devtools_sessionCount_other.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Session tab: how many elements the session names. $count$ is the number.

devtools_remove.description: DevTools, Piwi panel, Session tab: button beside a named element that takes it out of the session. One word.

stability_position.description: Name of a locator stability rule, in a list after “Brittle locator:”: the locator picks an element by its order (nth, first, last). Lower case, a few words.

stability_cssClass.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator finds an element by a CSS class. Lower case except acronyms.

stability_cssStructure.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator depends on the document’s structure (child combinators, nth-child).

stability_xpath.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator is an XPath.

stability_generatedId.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator uses an id a framework generates, which changes between builds.

stability_styleAttribute.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator matches the style or class attribute as a string.

stability_longText.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator matches an exact text over 40 characters.

stability_dataText.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator’s text holds a count, price or date, which changes with the data.

stability_deepChain.description: Name of a locator stability rule: the locator chains more than three locating calls.

codegen_noLocator.message: No locator was recorded for this element.
codegen_noLocator.description: Warning about a step of a generated test, after “Step N:”: the recorder found no way to locate the element.

codegen_brittleLocator.message: The best locator recorded for this element may break when the page changes: $locator$
codegen_brittleLocator.description: Warning about a step of a generated test. $locator$ is a Playwright locator, as code.

codegen_redactedValue.message: A password was typed here: the test reads it from $variable$.
codegen_redactedValue.description: Warning about a step of a generated test. $variable$ is the name of an environment variable, as code.

codegen_emptyAssertion.message: This check has nothing to compare.
codegen_emptyAssertion.description: Warning about a step of a generated test: an assertion step with no assertion in it.

codegen_missingExpected.description: Warning about a step of a generated test. $matcher$ is a Playwright matcher, as code.

codegen_fileNeeded.message: A file was chosen here ($files$): the test reads it from the folder Playwright runs in.
codegen_fileNeeded.description: A warning of the converter: a file was chosen at this step, and the generated test reads a file of that name. $files$ is the file names.

codegen_manualStep.description: A warning of the converter: a step of a steps file made from a test run is done by hand, and the generated test only names it in a comment. $step$ is the step's number, $description$ what to do (in English, from the file).

description.example: Open the page the test writes itself

common_actionExpectNot.description: Label of a negated assertion a test makes on an element (expect(…).not.toBeVisible()). $matcher$ is a Playwright matcher, as code.

bug_noScreenshotNone.description: Bug report, after “No screenshot:”: the reason when no screenshot was taken and nothing said why. Lower case.
